text:
Jordan - Support: Heads up — user in #help clicked an email titled 'Confirm your Okta sign-in' and approved an app consent. they say they didn't type password, just clicked the link. link: http://okta.reset-account[.]com/consent?id=abc123
Maria (EngSec): Which user? any screenshots or browser logs?
Jordan - Support: finance@redwood.com. attached screenshot (user pasted it in DM) — showed a permission screen asking to allow 'Redwood Account Manager' to access profile + openid + offline_access.
Alex R.: If they allowed offline_access we should assume refresh token possible. recommend revoke app and force SSO session reset for that user immediately.
Maria (EngSec): Agreed. Jordan, can you confirm whether the user copied/pasted any codes or uploaded files?
Jordan - Support: User says they only clicked "Allow" then closed tab. no files uploaded, no codes pasted into forms as far as they remember.
Maria (EngSec): OK. I'm going to run the link through our sandbox. Sam, can you queue a SIEM search for requests to okta.reset-account[.]com and any POSTs to that domain from company IPs in the last 24h? also search for recent OAuth token exchanges referencing that redirect.
Sam - SRE: On it.
Maria (EngSec): @PhishSandboxBot start http://okta.reset-account[.]com/consent?id=abc123
PhishSandboxBot: Sandbox run started: id=sbx-2026-04-10-77
PhishSandboxBot: Sandbox verdict: MALICIOUS. Summary: credential-harvest OAuth consent phishing. Flow captures OAuth code, immediately exchanges to obtain refresh token via malicious backend, then prompts victim to upload a JSON 'recovery file' (likely service account / key material) for "verification". domain registered 2026-04-09, TLS cert self-signed, multiple identical pages hosted under different subdomains.
Maria (EngSec): Yikes — that upload prompt is worrying. even if this user didn't upload, we should assume possible lateral impact if any service account or API keys were exposed elsewhere. Steps I recommend: 1) Revoke the malicious OAuth app in our IdP. 2) Force logout for finance@redwood.com and rotate any user tokens. 3) Revoke any service account keys that saw recent use + rotate KMS-access secrets if there's evidence. 4) SIEM search for file uploads to that domain and outgoing traffic to its IPs. 5) Incident ticket and notice to compliance + affected user comms.
Alex R.: I'll handle IdP revoke and global app block. Maria, can you paste the SIEM queries you want so Sam can run them exactly?
Maria (EngSec): SIEM queries (copy/paste):
```
http.request.host: "okta.reset-account.com" OR url:"okta.reset-account[.]com"
http.request.method: POST AND destination.domain: "okta.reset-account.com"
process.env.CONTENT_UPLOAD: * AND destination.ip in (list of sandbox IPs)
```
Sam - SRE: Running now. quick update: found 7 internal hosts that made HTTP(S) requests to that domain in last 6h. none of those have file upload artifacts in our object storage logs, but will dig deeper for multipart/form-data POST bodies in proxy logs.
Lena - Compliance: Please open an incident with severity = medium until we confirm no key exfil. if service-account JSONs were submitted we may need to notify customers depending on the project.
Jordan - Support: User confirmed they did NOT upload any file. they are happy to do a full device scan and change their SSO session.
Maria (EngSec): Good. Alex — once you revoke the app, please paste the revoke event id here. Sam — hold on rotating any org-wide KMS keys unless we find an upload. instead rotate any individual service account keys tied to hosts that contacted domain.
Alex R.: Done. IdP revoke event: event=evt-55012, app-blocked globally.
Sam - SRE: SIEM follow-up: of the 7 hosts, 5 are personal laptops (users clicked), 2 are CI runners. CI runners made a single outbound request from a sandboxed build container; no files attached. I ran a quick KMS-access query for those CI service accounts: no unusual decrypt requests in last 48h.
Maria (EngSec): Thanks. action items: 1) Alex — block app + add domain to org denylist (done). 2) Sam — rotate keys for any service accounts that had the malicious domain in access logs (you found none for KMS decrypts, so none for now). 3) Jordan — confirm user changed SSO session and completed device scan (they agreed). 4) Lena — open incident ticket and draft notification if we later find exfil.
Lena - Compliance: Incident opened: INC-2026-0427-03. I'll draft a short employee advisory to avoid clicking consent screens and remind to report.
Maria (EngSec): We'll add a short FAQ for finance folks about OAuth consent prompts and what to do. also recommend adding a rule to block newly-registered domains in our email gateway for 7 days if they request OAuth-like flows.
Jordan - Support: User says they're fine. they appreciated the quick response. :thumbsup:
PhishSandboxBot: Additional artifact: browser screenshot captured, backend IPs: 198.51.100.23, 198.51.100.24. vulnerability note: uses social engineering to request 'recovery json' — treat as high-risk for secret exposure.
Sam - SRE: Closing loop — proxy logs will keep 30d retention; I'll export the related flows to the incident ticket.
Maria (EngSec): Closing here — no evidence of credential material uploaded, app revoked, incident open, educ note planned. will update if SIEM finds anything new.
Jordan - Support: Thanks team!"
